cities.name: Austin
cities.role: Texas builders, operators, and engineering talent
cities.reason: A confident hometown invitation. The Texas character belongs here, and the message connects directly to work already happening on the ground.
cities.placement: Two standard bulletin faces for four weeks. Select routes near relevant employers and commuting corridors after inventory, sightline, and audience review.
cities.proof: An Austin field demonstration and an approved Texas job-site story.

cities.name: Boston
cities.role: Robotics, autonomy, controls, and systems engineers
cities.reason: Lead with the work a technical audience can own. Plain workwear replaces the scally cap and shamrock; the ambition carries the local relevance.
cities.placement: Candidate specialist market after the Austin review. Quote employer and university corridors; select inventory for the hiring brief, not a landmark.
cities.proof: A technical session with the engineers building Mission Control. All roles and relocation details must be current.

cities.name: San Francisco
cities.reason: Make the consequence of the work tangible: software that reaches the physical world. Keep the language direct and the character consistent.
cities.placement: Consider only when role demand supports the market. Standard formats first; premium skyline placements require a separate business case.
cities.proof: A short, approved code-to-machine demonstration with a named engineering role.

cities.name: Los Angeles
cities.role: Aerospace, hardware, and advanced systems talent
cities.reason: A future-facing invitation that works honestly with illustration. It does not make a photographic-proof claim that the artwork cannot support.
cities.placement: Evaluate aerospace and engineering corridors before entertainment districts. No Sunset Strip commitment.
cities.proof: Show real hardware, real teammates, and the connection between engineering decisions and field results.

cities.name: Chicago
cities.role: Industrial systems, equipment, and field operations talent
cities.reason: Give the city a serious industrial invitation. The plain hardhat signals the work without relying on food jokes or costume.
cities.placement: Industrial and technical commuter routes, subject to hiring demand and audience evidence.
cities.proof: An operator-and-engineer story about moving a project from plan to ground.

cities.name: Nashville
cities.role: Builders, equipment specialists, and operations talent
cities.reason: Use the national mission line where a stronger local truth has not been established. No rhinestones or tourist-landmark setup is needed.
cities.placement: A future role-led test, not a mandatory stop on a national tour.
cities.proof: Texas work today, with Mars clearly identified as the long-term ambition.

cities.name: Miami
cities.reason: A concise invitation to build the future, with Texas stated in the action line. Use a fluent local copy review before production.
cities.placement: Test Spanish and English variants with the actual target audience before selecting a language or buying inventory.
cities.proof: A bilingual recruiting journey with matching role requirements and no unsupported relocation promise.

cities.name: New York
cities.reason: Keep the strongest city observation: every skyline depends on groundwork. The headline receives three short lines and no decorative script.
cities.placement: Relevant commuter inventory before Times Square. No Williamsburg poster package is hidden inside the Austin budget.
cities.proof: An approved before-and-after site story, with the people and machinery behind it.

cities.name: Washington, DC
cities.reason: Keep the mission clear without a suit, security badge, or visual implication of government endorsement.
cities.placement: Technical employer corridors only if the recruiting brief supports a dedicated market test.
cities.proof: Approved capabilities and open roles; no implied clearance requirement or government affiliation.

cities.name: Atlanta
cities.reason: Connect digital ambition to physical construction in five words. Plain workwear keeps the focus on the idea.
cities.placement: Evaluate infrastructure and technical commuter audiences, rather than adding a stop just to complete the map.
cities.proof: A verified infrastructure story. Do not imply an unannounced data-center customer or contract.
